questions.question_text: What do the ACID properties guarantee for a database transaction? Briefly explain each property.
questions.reference_answer:
ACID describes reliability guarantees for transactions.
Atomicity: a transaction is all-or-nothing — either every operation commits, or on failure the system rolls back so it looks like the transaction never happened.
Consistency: a committed transaction takes the database from one valid state to another, preserving integrity constraints (keys, checks, business rules).
Isolation: concurrent transactions do not interfere; the effect is as if transactions ran one after another (serializable, or at least their intermediate states are hidden per the isolation level).
Durability: once a transaction commits, its effects survive crashes/power loss (typically via logging / stable storage).
questions.rubric:
Total 4 marks (1 mark each; concepts stay atomic even though the stem is one line):
1) Atomicity: all-or-nothing / commit all ops or rollback.
2) Consistency: preserves integrity constraints / valid state to valid state.
3) Isolation: concurrent transactions do not see each other's uncommitted/intermediate effects (serializable idea OK).
4) Durability: committed data survives failure / persisted to stable storage.
Partial credit (0.5) if partially correct.
Award 0 if absent, swaps definitions wrongly with no recovery, or contradictory.

student_answers.answer_text: Atomicity means the transaction is all-or-nothing: either all changes commit or the DBMS rolls everything back on failure. Consistency means after commit the database still satisfies its integrity constraints — it moves from one valid state to another. Isolation means concurrent transactions do not interfere; each behaves as if it ran alone (or at least does not see dirty intermediate states). Durability means once committed, the results survive a crash because they are written to stable storage / the log.

A = all operations succeed or none (rollback). C = constraints/rules still hold after the transaction. I = transactions appear not to step on each other while running together. D = committed updates are permanent even after power loss.
